instruction: A 200-year-old male grandpa with a gravelly, raspy, sharply nasal tenor-baritone voice. Clearly ancient and frail: thin, dry throat; weak breath support; slight tremor; wavering pitch; mild vocal fry; occasional voice cracks. Keep a worn midrange with a pinched nasal edge—not youthful, smooth, bright, booming, or bass-heavy. Weary and very, VERY drunk; intoxicated muttering, lazy half-swallowed slurred words, irregular interrupted tempo, sharp cynical emphasis, stumbling breath, and sudden explosive manic delight. Perform like a frail old alcoholic portal scientist: slur and stumble through the words, pause and lose your train of thought, then snap into manic scientific certainty. Keep every word intelligible.
text: Retirement lasted eleven minutes, then the boredom became unbearable. So I built a pocket-sized arena and started collecting the greatest fighters in every universe.
